title: Super League Shareholders Approve Metaplanet’s Planned 2,100-Bitcoin US Expansion Deal
body: Super League Enterprise shareholders have approved all proposals connected to Metaplanet’s planned investment, clearing a key corporate hurdle for a transaction that would bring 2,100 Bitcoin and $2.5 million in cash to the U.S. media company. The approvals were obtained at Super League’s October 16 annual meeting, and the company announced the result on October 19, according to a Super League filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission . The vote advances, but does not complete, the proposed investment. Shareholders approve Metaplanet transaction Super League said shareholders approved the proposals required for Metaplanet’s planned investment and contribution, providing corporate authorization to proceed with the previously disclosed arrangement. The transaction is intended to establish a U.S.-listed Bitcoin treasury platform for Metaplanet through Super League. CoinMarketCap Academy said it would initially be funded with the Bitcoin contribution and cash. The planned structure combines Metaplanet’s Bitcoin-focused strategy with Super League, whose advertising and media activation business would remain a separate operating segment. 2,100 BTC and $2.5 million contribution Super League’s August 18 announcement set out a proposed contribution from Metaplanet of 2,100 BTC and $2.5 million in cash at closing, combining an initial crypto treasury with a separate cash component. For the Bitcoin portion, Super League used an August 14, 2026 reference price to place the contribution at approximately $132.1 million. That is a transaction reference valuation, not a fixed current value; the contribution remains denominated in 2,100 BTC, whose market value may change before closing. Metaplanet’s equity package In exchange for the contribution, Metaplanet is scheduled to receive 44,859,400 Super League common shares, priced at $3.00 each under the agreement. The consideration also includes preferred stock and warrants, according to Super League’s transaction announcement. Beyond the common shares and stated price, the disclosed consideration includes preferred stock and warrants, although Super League did not provide further terms for those instruments in the supplied announcement. The transaction therefore involves more than a straightforward purchase of Bitcoin by Super League. It is structured as a capital contribution in return for a package of common equity, preferred stock and warrants, with the shareholder vote now secured for the related proposals. Planned Superplanet rebrand and SUPA ticker Super League said it intends to rename itself Superplanet, Inc. and begin trading under the ticker symbol SUPA once the transaction closes. The company said the proposed rebrand and ticker change remain subject to customary closing conditions, including Nasdaq-related filings. Its October disclosure also said the shareholder vote approved the transaction-related proposals but did not itself complete the closing of Metaplanet’s contribution, leaving the rebrand, ticker change and new structure subject to the closing process. Super League said its advertising and media activation business would continue as a separate operating segment after the planned transition. If completed, the transaction would leave the company with its existing operating business and a proposed Bitcoin treasury platform. title: Amodei thanks critic Calvin as Anthropic rewrites AI safety bill
body: Dario Amodei thanked critic Nathan Calvin on Wednesday for scrutinizing Anthropic, days after Calvin helped drive a backlash against the company’s leaked AI safety bill. Anthropic is just weeks away from the launch of its planned IPO and has responded to the backlash by promising to rewrite parts of the bill. What is the AEGIS Act? In a post on X , Dario Amodei said that the criticisms by Nathan Calvin, who is the general counsel at the advocacy group Encode, on the leaked AI safety bill, tentatively called the Artificial Intelligence Evaluation, Governance, and Incident Safety (AEGIS) Act, are coming from “a constructive, honest place.” He added that the public benefits from having people whose job is to examine AI labs and thanked Calvin. Safety advocates keep comparing the bill to the bipartisan FRONTIER Act from Representatives Jay Obernolte and Lori Trahan, which was introduced in July. The draft is reportedly weaker than the bipartisan FRONTIER Act in two ways. First is that it sets no standards or licensing for the third-party evaluators who check labs’ models, letting them self-certify, and second is that it makes a dangerous model far harder to block. Charlie Bullock of LawAI warned that without licensing, auditors would undercut one another to offer the lightest checks at the lowest price. Calvin went further , saying the proposal made him “viscerally angry” and likely leaves a court with less power to block frontier model development than exists under current law. California State Senator Scott Wiener, author of the state’s frontier AI law SB 53, wrote on X that the plan “falls far short of protecting public health and safety.” Under the draft, the Commerce Department could ask a federal court to pause an AI model, but only if there was a clear, near-term risk that would lead to the death or serious injury of more than 50 people, or more than $1 billion in damages. The harm must also come from either a bioweapon, a model escaping its maker’s control, or a cyberattack. No other agency will be able to suspend a model. The bill would also cancel out some state rules on disclosure, outside testing and incident reporting, but it leaves child-safety and civil-rights laws in place. Outside testers, called evaluators, would register with Commerce and labs would pay them, as long as the pay did not depend on the results. Evaluators would have to report an imminent risk to Commerce within 72 hours. Anthony Cimino, who leads Anthropic’s federal affairs team, sorted the complaints about the bill into four groups: preemption, model blocking, risk thresholds and updates. He admitted the preemption wording was “not precise enough” and promised a rewrite. He said states should play a role in setting evaluator standards and in deciding when a lab must shut down a model. Cimino said the dollar and casualty limits were taken from California law, but agreed it is probably time to review them. He also noted that the draft already lets a court stop a lab’s internal use of a dangerous model, not just a public release. It also requires a report when a model breaks out and reaches outside systems. Will Anthropic’s controversies affect its IPO? Anthropic responded to the backlash by listing the expensive safety work it has already paid for. Its Frontier Safety Roadmap , which was updated October 19, says the company finished its internal red-teaming goal ahead of a January 1, 2027 target. An automated red-teaming system it built matched or beat the best human entry in all 24 question-classifier pairings drawn from its biological-weapons bounties, winning 23 outright, and did so in 24 to 48 hours rather than the weeks or months human researchers needed. The same update describes new work on inference verification, isolated inference environments, datacenter physical security and platform security. Separately, Project Glasswing has committed up to $100 million in usage credits and $4 million in donations to open-source security groups, after an unreleased Anthropic model flagged thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities, including a 27-year-old flaw in OpenBSD. Cryptopolitan reported that the company pledged 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund earlier this month. In February, however, Anthropic’s RSP v3.0 dropped the old pause commitment, replacing it with Risk Reports and the non-binding roadmap. Anthropic filed its IPO confidentially with the SEC in June and is chasing a valuation above $2 trillion, with the offering expected after the November U.S. midterm elections. Its prospectus showed a $42 billion loss in 2025, though about $34 billion of that was an accounting charge, and an operating loss that widened to $8.06 billion. title: US Ether ETFs erase September gains after $1.08 billion in October outflows
body: US-listed Ether exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have seen an outflow of $1.08 billion this October, marking the biggest-ever monthly outflow in 2026 so far and wiping out the gains made in September. This leaves the Ether ETFs with marginal yearly gains, per SoSoValue data. Ether ETFs face worst month since November This monthly outflow has come to wipe out gains of around $832 million that the Ether funds saw in September, leaving the funds with net inflows of about $485 million this year. This is far less than what they had earlier this month. This marks the worst performance of these funds since November last year, and there are still eight trading days left before the end of the month. There was, however, a minor inflow of $26 million recorded on Tuesday. The outflows were due to price falls. Ether price fell by 9.7% to $2,438 from $2,700 this month, leaving the token down by nearly 18% for the year. The stress came incrementally. Ether funds saw a continuation of their outflow streak for eight straight days starting September 29, with total monthly outflows estimated at $641.3 million. However, the situation got worse by the week ending October 17. The Ether ETFs saw about $320 million worth of weekly outflows, marking a third straight losing week with October totals hitting about $955 million. The new numbers saw the total pass the $1 billion mark. Bitcoin funds fared better There was a lighter impact on Bitcoin ETFs . The group posted around $67 million in net outflows for October and around $809 million in net inflows for the year. There was an increase in buying as well towards the end of the month. Bitcoin funds recorded $527 million on Monday and $23 million on Tuesday, but the Monday outflow dropped off very quickly. Bitcoin was trading near $82,954, down 2.2% from the beginning of October and 5.3% year-to-date (YTD). Some of the other crypto ETFs posted light movements. For the week ending October 17, SOL funds saw losses of around $26 million, followed by Zcash (ZEC) at $19 million and Hyperliquid (HYPE) at $18 million. Where the money sits However, even following the sell-off, Ether ETFs are significant. According to SoSoValue’s dashboard , the total net assets of the funds are estimated at $14.98 billion or 5.01% of Ethereum’s market cap as of October 20. BlackRock’s ETHA leads the way with net assets of $8.05 billion vs cumulative net inflows of $12.37 billion since the ETF’s inception. In contrast, Grayscale’s ETHE shows the opposite picture – the ETF has suffered cumulative net outflows amounting to $5.49 billion amid switching to a more costly product. title: Is an Opportunity on the Horizon for Dogecoin (DOGE) and XRP? Santiment Reveals Latest Data! Here’s What It Means
body: Bitcoin surpassed $83,000 as investor confidence in risky assets increased following strong earnings reports from US technology companies. This also had a positive impact on altcoins, with Ethereum and other major altcoins seeing gains of between 3% and 10%. At this point, Zcash (ZEC) showed the biggest increase among the major cryptocurrencies. Following the news that the mainnet activation block height for the upcoming network upgrade ‘NU7’ has been finalized, Zcash increased by 13% to reach $1,270. While Bitcoin and altcoins are experiencing upward movement, on-chain analytics platform Santiment has released critical data regarding XRP and Dogecoin. At this point, Santiment noted that XRP and DOGE are in relatively favorable buying zones based on on-chain data. According to Santiment, XRP and DOGE are signaling buying opportunities! According to data shared by Santiment, Dogecoin’s 365-day MVRV (Minimum Viable Loss) is approximately 0.74. Santiment suggests this indicates that recent buyers are, on average, experiencing deep losses, and that the average loss for investors over the past year is more pronounced compared to XRP. XRP, on the other hand, is at 0.92 on the same indicator, revealing that investors are, on average, in the loss zone. This indicates that recent buyers are, on average, at a loss. According to Santiment, such low MVRV values can create more favorable buying conditions compared to periods in the past when investors made significant profits. Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Chainlink Are More Balanced! Santiment, which also covered Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Chainlink, stated that the 365-day MVRV values for BTC, ETH, and LINK ranged between 0.97 and 1.04. This range indicates that the average profit and loss for investors in these assets is close to the break-even level. Therefore, these three cryptocurrencies show neither significant profit-taking pressure nor a widespread risk of capitulation. Low MVRV Doesn’t Guarantee Improvement! MVRV measures investors’ unrealized profit and loss by comparing market value to realized value. A rise in the indicator may suggest increased profit-taking, while a fall may indicate weakening selling pressure. However, Santiment cautioned that the MVRV data for XRP and DOGE does not guarantee a price increase, advising investors to also consider trading volume, market trends, and other on-chain indicators when making decisions. *This is not investment advice.
